explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/437: can there be more than x^{1−ε} square partial products, for every ε > 0? Yes (BPZ24, via Tao). L x is the maximum number of square partial products a₁⋯a_i of a strictly increasing list in [1,x], as on erdosproblems.com/437; the set is bounded by x, so the sSup is a maximum. The statement: for every ε > 0, eventually x^{1−ε} < L x. Faithful.
